name: IntuneStatefulDeviceFingerprinting
description: KuShu-Shimon Intune Stateful Device Fingerprinting (ISDF) provides a tamper-resistant device fingerprint for enrolled Windows devices, enforced via Intune Custom Compliance and DPAPI-encrypted baselines. In Cloud mode it attests fingerprints to Entra ID through APIM and a Logic App to enable trusted device filters, dynamic groups, and stronger Conditional Access policies. The solution collects on-device signals, stores encrypted baselines, self-heals missing keys, and reports ISDF booleans for compliant state.
author: Graham Hild

securityCheck.aiSummary: The codebase includes legitimate Intune/Azure discovery and telemetry components but exhibits notable security-relevant patterns: encoded/obfuscated inline commands in watchdog for persistence, a SYSTEM-level scheduled task for ongoing execution, and cloud-based telemetry exfiltration via webhooks. There are no hardcoded secrets. Recommend auditing the use of encoded commands, tightening registry and scheduled task access, validating webhook trust, and ensuring that telemetry is scoped to necessary data with explicit user/organizational consent.

noObfuscatedCode.reason: Inline PowerShell payload is encoded with Base64 via -EncodedCommand for the scheduled task. This obfuscation conceals behavior and can hinder auditing and review. It also enables automated persistence-like execution on multiple triggers.
